data.title: Plant Power: Leaf Cell Builder
data.description: Build a working plant cell by placing the correct parts in the right places and matching their jobs!

organelles.name: Nucleus
organelles.function: Acts as the brain of the cell and holds the instruction manual.
organelles.analogy: Like the principal's office of a school.
organelles.quantityReasoning: A plant cell only needs one main control center to direct all its daily activities.

organelles.name: Mitochondria
organelles.function: Turns food into energy the cell can use.
organelles.analogy: Like a power plant for the cell.
organelles.quantityReasoning: Leaf cells need some energy to run their processes, but they also get energy from sunlight.

organelles.name: Chloroplast
organelles.function: Captures sunlight to make food for the plant.
organelles.quantityReasoning: Leaf cells need lots of chloroplasts because their main job is to capture sunlight for making food.

organelles.name: Large Central Vacuole
organelles.function: Stores water and helps keep the plant crisp and firm.
organelles.analogy: Like a giant water storage tank.
organelles.quantityReasoning: Plant cells use one giant storage tank to hold water and keep the plant from wilting.

organelles.name: Cytoplasm
organelles.function: Fills the cell and keeps all the parts floating in place.
organelles.quantityReasoning: The cell needs enough jelly-like filling throughout to cushion and support all internal parts.

organelles.name: Cell Membrane
organelles.function: Controls what goes in and out of the cell.
organelles.analogy: Like a security guard at the door.
organelles.quantityReasoning: One continuous boundary is needed to wrap around the entire cell.

organelles.name: Centrioles
organelles.function: Help organize cell division in animal cells.
organelles.analogy: Like construction workers setting up scaffolding.
organelles.distractorExplanation: Centrioles are mostly found in animal cells, not plant cells.

functionMatches.functionDescription: Stores the genetic blueprint and directs all cellular activities.
Breaks down nutrients to supply usable power for cellular tasks.
Absorbs light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into sugars.
Maintains internal pressure by holding water and dissolved materials.
Provides a fluid medium where organelles are suspended and protected.
Selectively lets helpful substances pass through while blocking unwanted items.

cellMembrane.description: A flexible outer layer surrounding the cell contents.
cellMembrane.function: Regulates the movement of water, nutrients, and waste into and out of the cell.

cellWall.description: A tough, rigid outer layer made of cellulose that sits outside the cell membrane.
